facts.statement: The type locality of Gondwananectes is the Quehuita Formation in Chile.
Gondwananectes lived during the Middle Jurassic Bajocian age.
The fossil material of Gondwananectes was discovered by Osvaldo Rojas and his team in 2014 at the Ojo Opache locality, about 10 km west of Calama in northern Chile.
facts.quote: The Gondwananectes fossil material was discovered by Osvaldo Rojas, who collected it with a team of paleontologists in 2014. The bones were found at the Ojo Opache locality, representing outcrops of the Quehuita Formation, a site situated 10 km west of Calama in Antofagasta Region, northern Chile.

facts.statement: Later preparation showed the previously interpreted pelvic bones were actually parts of the pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: revealed that these pelvic bones were actually part of the pectoral girdle.

facts.statement: The holotype preserves several articulated cervical vertebrae, partial pectoral and dorsal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, coracoids, scapulae, and possibly ilium fragments.
facts.quote: Full preparation revealed that the extent of preserved material comprises several articulated cervical (neck) vertebrae and partial pectoral and dorsal (trunk) vertebrae, several ribs and gastralia], part of the pectoral girdle (coracoids and scapulae), and badly damaged bones that may be part of the ilium

facts.statement: The preserved cervical and dorsal vertebrae are about 30 cm long each.
facts.quote: As preserved, the articulated cervical and dorsal vertebrae measure about 30 cm long.

facts.statement: Based on the pelvic girdle, the trunk region likely measured around 60 cm, and the humerus suggests a forelimb length of 60–70 cm.
facts.quote: Based on the postulated pelvic girdle morphology, the trunk region likely measured 60 cm. Similarly, the humerus size implies a 60 - 70 cm-long forelimb.

facts.statement: Gondwananectes is estimated to have been 1.5–2 m long in total body length.
facts.quote: In combination, the total body length was likely between 1.5 and 2 m.

facts.statement: It likely possessed 29–39 cervical vertebrae and 20–23 dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Gondwananectes likely had around 29–39 cervical vertebrae adn 20–23 dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The degree of vertebral fusion indicates the holotype was a subadult nearing maturity at death.
facts.quote: Based on some degree of vertebral fusion in the holotype individual, it was not an especially young animal when it died. It was likely a subadult, nearing maturity.

facts.statement: PBDB records Gondwananectes from the Bajocian stage, about 170.9 to 168.2 million years ago, with a single occurrence.
facts.quote:
Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.2 million years ago)
Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
